milestones.title: Tales from Bellavere and Lindenfeld
milestones.text: The expanded edition of the story collection, in ebook and paperback.

milestones.title: “The Attic Record” in Half and One
milestones.text: A short story of memory and music, set in Lindenfeld in 1958, published in the fiction section of the online magazine Half and One on 10 October 2026.

milestones.title: Guest Composer, URI Composers’ Concert
milestones.text: Featured guest composer at the Spring 2026 Composers’ Concert of the University of Rhode Island, 8 pm in the URI Fine Arts Center Concert Hall, alongside new works by URI composition students under the guidance of Dr. Eliane Aberdam. Original piano works were performed.

milestones.title: “Wheat for the Living” in The Hamilton Stone Review
milestones.text: A short story published in Issue 54 of The Hamilton Stone Review, an independent literary journal.

milestones.title: #6, Euro Indie Music Chart
milestones.text: “Lets Dance (VS Pop™)” reached number 6 in week 6 of the weekly Euro Indie Music Chart, published by the European Indie Music Network. Earlier singles reached #6 (“Never Let You Go”, August 2025) and #10 (“Don’t Waste My Time”, December 2025).

milestones.title: FM Airplay in Chicago, and 19 College Radio Adds
milestones.text: “Dancing in the Dark” was tracked by Mediabase on WCPY-FM Dance Factory, Chicago, with 57 spins between 18 April and 3 May 2025. In the same month the Official Electronic EP was added by 19 NACC-reporting college stations in the United States and Canada, reaching medium rotation at WDWN, WSUW and KXSU.

milestones.title: EARMILK on “Dancing in the Dark”
milestones.text: The music publication EARMILK featured the VS Pop™ single “Dancing in the Dark”.

milestones.title: #1, Moon Phase Radio Ambient Top 10
milestones.text: “Ghosa (The Call)” topped the weekly Ambient Channel Top 10 of the independent station Moon Phase Radio on 13 and 20 January 2025. The station’s charts are based on listener interactions.

milestones.title: 46 Works on IMSLP
milestones.text: Symphonies, string quartets, fugues, sonatas, piano, chamber and orchestral works, published with free scores on the International Music Score Library Project.

items.title: CR Srikanth lights up the night with “Dancing in the Dark - VS Pop™”
‘Dancing in the Dark – VS Pop™’ by CR Srikanth
Formula Indie Sessions: Interview with CR Srikanth
C.R. Srikanth
items.type: Podcast · 23 min · a musical journey and the history of Indian music

items.title: Bridging Western & Indian Classical Music: VS Pop™ Orchestral Thinking

bio: CR Srikanth, also known as Ravi Chandra Srikanth Cherukupalli, is a composer, recording artist, writer of literary fiction and builder of tools for musical creation. He works across all four, and treats them as one practice: different ways for the same imagination to take form.

As a composer he works between traditions. His musical foundation is in Western classical music as well as Carnatic and Hindustani music, and the influence of all three runs through a catalogue he numbers by opus: symphonies such as Pi and Hope, string quartets, nocturnes, sonatas, fugues, études, waltzes and a long series of symphonic serenades. Selected scores are published for free on IMSLP, the International Music Score Library Project, and in spring 2026 his piano works were performed at the University of Rhode Island Composers’ Concert, where he was the guest composer. He completed Berklee Online’s Music Composition for Film and TV 2 and is a registered ASCAP composer and publisher.

As a recording artist he created VS Pop™, short for Very Smooth Pop: songs that join pop songwriting and electronic production to cinematic textures and orchestral colour. VS Pop™ releases are distributed worldwide, have been played on college, community and FM radio in several countries, and have appeared on independent charts.

As an author he writes literary fiction about memory, family, identity, moral choice and the passage of time. His stories have been published by The Hamilton Stone Review and Half and One. His books, published in 2026, include the collection Tales from Bellavere and Lindenfeld, the novella The Debt of the Fifth Month, and the novels August 18th, GOTTESGABE, Kamil & Hassan Drama Company and The House on the Hill Above the River. Several of them share towns and families, so they can be read as one connected world.

As an innovator he builds the tools he wants as a composer. A software architect by profession, he has spent years on algorithmic composition, counterpoint and raga engines, and now on CuTTI: CuTTI Studio, an assistant arranger that turns a brief or a score into a ready-to-work session in the DAW, and CuTTI Score, which turns printed music into editable, playable scores. Both are private and in active development, and both rest on one principle: the composer stays in charge.

dimensions.title: The Composer
dimensions.text: Classical foundations in Western, Carnatic and Hindustani music; symphonies, quartets, fugues, piano and chamber works catalogued by opus, with selected scores on IMSLP.

dimensions.title: The Recording Artist
dimensions.text: VS Pop™, Very Smooth Pop: contemporary songs with cinematic textures and orchestral colour, distributed on the major platforms.

dimensions.title: The Author
dimensions.text: Literary fiction in independent magazines, a story collection, a novella and novels, many of them set in the same imagined towns.

dimensions.title: The Innovator
dimensions.text: CuTTI Studio and CuTTI Score: private studio tools that take on the drudgery between an idea and a working session.

privacy: This website is run by CR Srikanth. It does not use advertising, analytics or tracking cookies.

If you use the contact form, your name, email address and message are sent by email to CR Srikanth so that he can reply. They are not shared with anyone else, sold or used for marketing, and they are deleted when they are no longer needed for the conversation.

Videos and Spotify players are shown as still images and buttons until you choose to play. Only then does your browser load the player from YouTube (youtube-nocookie.com) or Spotify, under their own privacy policies. Links to streaming services, bookstores and magazines take you to those sites, which have their own policies.
Fonts are loaded from Google Fonts. To ask what information is held about you, or to have it deleted, email crs.07@crsrikanth.com.
